refined_contract.contract: Simulator time must be supplied through an injected deterministic clock. SimulationClock is V1 evidence; V2 already owns a Clock port. Stage 21.15.3b must resolve the adapter mapping and enumerate any simulator path that still reads wall-clock time directly.

One caller-supplied seed must determine a run. SimulationRng owns seeded draws, draw count and state evidence in V1; V2 RandomSource remains the application port. Global/module random injection is compatibility evidence and must be scoped and restored, not treated as a preferred V2 boundary.

A simulation run must use isolated state or explicit in-memory/fake repositories and must not open accumulated production game.db state. No adapter may silently fall back to production SQLite, shared mutable globals, or live Telegram/runtime state.

Simulator repositories must satisfy existing V2 repository and Unit-of-Work contracts. A run has explicit begin/commit-or-rollback semantics in its sandbox; production repository adapters and direct SQL are not simulator defaults.

Simulator adapters orchestrate production domain/application services. They must not duplicate combat, derived-stat, equipment-generation, enhancement, durability, EXP, reward, loot or repair formulas when an authoritative production owner exists.
Existing for_simulator factories are approved reuse seams only for the behavior they explicitly construct. They do not authorize parallel formula implementations or production persistence access.

Fixtures must be deterministic, minimal and explicit for accounts, characters, primary stats, equipment, runes, resources and encounters. Existing numeric fixture values are evidence, not new production content or balance policy.

Same configuration, seed, clock and fixture must reproduce the same result and draw/state evidence. Failed runs must discard sandbox mutations; retries must start from a fresh fixture rather than partially reused state.

Reports may describe deterministic inputs, outputs, seed, clock, draw counts and warnings. Reporting must not mutate production state or promote sandbox candidate settings to canonical gameplay policy.
Any Stage 21.15.3 implementation must use the flat module rom_v2/domain/simulator_adapters.py. A nested rom_v2/domain/simulator_adapters package is not authorized.

superseded_interpretations: Keyword evidence alone does not establish simulator ownership.
Direct SQL in legacy systems is not an approved simulator repository adapter.
Global random or temporary module injection is not the preferred V2 RNG boundary.
Sandbox candidate parameters are not canonical live balance policy.
Simulator-local formula copies are not authoritative where production domain/application owners exist.

unresolved_for_parity.reason: Resolve exact SimulationClock-to-Clock semantics, start instant, advance rules and all remaining wall-clock reads used by simulator paths.
Resolve the exact seeded source, supported draw methods, draw-count/state-digest contract, and every global/module random compatibility injection that must be eliminated or safely restored.
Map each simulator state mutation to an isolated repository/UoW or pure state owner and prove that production SQLite cannot be selected implicitly.
For combat, stats, equipment, enhancement, loot, EXP, rewards, repair and survival, identify the exact authoritative production callable and every simulator duplicate or compatibility copy.
Resolve canonical deterministic fixture builders and which numeric values are parity fixtures rather than production defaults or new content.
Resolve run begin, success, failure, rollback, retry and report-write boundaries, including whether reports survive a failed sandbox run.
Identify candidate-only PvP/balance sandboxes and prevent their parameters from being interpreted as approved live policy.
